findings.reason: the section's write-path list decides where the worker may write, so as written it forces a second, CLI-local implementation of a check s2 says must exist once in `validate_node`.
findings.text: s3 requires an implement-role brief dispatch with neither flag to be refused "at dispatch ... on the single path and for a batch entry", but its declared write paths are `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py`, `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py` and the new test: they omit `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` and `reckon/crew/node.py`, the two files where a single-path contract refusal can live once s2 has moved the contract into the whole-node judge. A worker obeying s3 literally must either write the single-path refusal into the CLI (`crew_run_commands.py`) — which reintroduces exactly the duplicated-refusal split s2 exists to remove, and leaves the batch and single paths judged by two different implementations — or write outside its fence.

findings.reason: the section already requires a temporary repository for the test, which implies the flag; the fix is one clause naming `--repo <temp repo>` on the dry-run invocation, and a worker reaching the failure sees the guard directly.
findings.text: s2's sixth bullet ("For each refused entry, the single path's `--dry-run` of the same node reports the same detail") cannot be satisfied for the fourth entry as stated: `plan_dispatch` only runs `gate_population_finding` when `repo is not None` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:861`), and `--repo` defaults to `None`, so a dry run naming only the temporary crew home reports nothing for the glob population and the assertion fails or is silently weakened. The section does say the test uses "a temporary crew home and repository", but never says the dry run must be handed `--repo` to reach it.
